sourcedFrom: SIG SAUER P211 — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — 5100230-01 — part number printed on the document (2025)
cleanIntro: The P211 is SIG's double-stack 1911 — SIG's own words are that it is "designed from the foundation of the classic 1911 and adapted to accomodate a double stack magazine". It strips like a 1911 and carries a 1911's two hazards. The hammer must be COCKED before anything moves, and SIG forbids lowering it by pressing the trigger and easing it down. The recoil spring comes out under load. One P211-specific catch: older pistols have a slide catch PIN that must not be removed, and older slide catches need a 1/16-inch punch where newer ones do not.

steps.title: ⛔ Unload and clear — then check the hammer is COCKED
steps.action: Unload and clear the pistol and remove the magazine. Then confirm the hammer is cocked and disengage the manual safety. A 1911-pattern pistol will not strip with the hammer down, and forcing the point is how frames get marked.
steps.prose: Cocked, on an empty gun, with the safety off. That combination feels wrong to people and is exactly what the procedure asks for.
steps.aside: The SIG SAUER P211® pistol is a modern pistol designed from the foundation of the classic 1911 and adapted to accomodate a double stack magazine.
steps.quote: Ensure that the hammer is cocked. 3. Disengage the manual safety.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER P211 — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — 5100230-01 — part number printed on the document — Field strip the pistol, printed p.26

steps.title: ⛔ NEVER lower the hammer with the trigger
steps.action: SIG's warning is unambiguous: do not lower the hammer by pressing the trigger and easing it forward. Doing so prevents the full application of the pistol's safety features. If the hammer is down, cock it — do not ride it down.
steps.prose: This is the habit a lot of 1911 owners bring with them, and it is the one SIG prints in capitals.
steps.quote: DO NOT ATTEMPT TO LOWER THE HAMMER OF THIS PISTOL BY PRESSING THE TRIGGER AND EASING THE HAMMER FORWARD. MANUALLY LOWERING THE HAMMER IN THIS MANNER PREVENTS THE FULL APPLICATION OF THE SAFETY FEATURES OF THIS PISTOL.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER P211 — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — 5100230-01 — part number printed on the document — Field strip the pistol, printed p.26

steps.title: Slide back until the slide catch LUG aligns with the disassembly notch
steps.action: Pull the slide to the rear and line the lug of the slide catch lever up with the DISASSEMBLY notch on the slide — not the slide-lock notch. Hold that alignment; the catch will not come out of any other position.
steps.prose: On a 1911 pattern there are two notches and only one of them releases the catch. Find it by alignment, not by force.
steps.quote: Pull the slide to the rear and align the lug of the slide catch lever with the disassembly notch on the slide.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER P211 — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — 5100230-01 — part number printed on the document — Field strip the pistol, printed p.27

steps.title: ⛔ Press the LEFT slide catch out through the RIGHT-side opening
steps.action: Press the left-side slide catch lever out of the frame, through the opening in the right-side lever. On older P211s the catch needs a 1/16-inch pin punch; newer ones do not. If yours resists, check which you have before reaching for a bigger tool.
steps.prose: Two generations of the same part, one of which needs a punch. SIG prints both and shows both.
steps.caution: Older P211 slide catches require the use of a 1/16th-in. pin punch to remove the slide catch lever.
steps.aside: IF PRESENT, DO NOT REMOVE THE SLIDE CATCH PIN. FAILURE TO COMPLY MAY RESULT IN DAMAGE TO THE FIREARM. THE SLIDE CATCH PIN IS PRESENT ON OLDER P211 PISTOLS.
steps.quote: Press the left side slide catch lever out of the frame through the opening in the right side slide catch lever.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER P211 — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — 5100230-01 — part number printed on the document — Field strip the pistol, printed p.27

steps.title: ⛔ Slide FORWARD off the frame — keep a grip on the spring guide
steps.action: Pull the slide assembly forward off the frame while keeping hold of the spring guide. The recoil system is not captive on this pistol; let go and it goes. Eye protection on, as SIG asks for any maintenance.
steps.prose: "While maintaining grip on the spring guide" is doing real work in that sentence.
steps.caution: DO NOT DRY FIRE THE PISTOL WITH THE SLIDE REMOVED. FAILURE TO COMPLY WILL DAMAGE THE REAR OF THE FRAME.
steps.quote: Pull the slide assembly forward off of the frame while maintaining grip on the spring guide.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER P211 — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — 5100230-01 — part number printed on the document — Field strip the pistol, printed p.28

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide FORWARD, then up and over the barrel link
steps.action: Push the recoil spring and spring guide forward slightly, then lift them up and over the barrel link. Take the spring off the guide rod, remove the recoil plug from the slide, and rotate the barrel link forward so the barrel will come out.
steps.prose: The barrel link has to be rotated out of the way; it is what the slide catch pin passed through.
steps.aside: Remove the recoil plug from the slide and rotate the barrel link forward.
steps.quote: Push the recoil spring and spring guide forward slightly, then lift them up and over the barrel link.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER P211 — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — 5100230-01 — part number printed on the document — Field strip the pistol, printed p.29

steps.title: Field strip complete — and do NOT dry fire it like this
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring, guide and plug. With the slide off, do not press the trigger: SIG states plainly that dry firing with the slide removed WILL damage the rear of the frame — not may, will.
steps.prose: It is an easy thing to do absent-mindedly with a frame in one hand. The damage is to the frame, which is the serialised part.
steps.quote: DO NOT DRY FIRE THE PISTOL WITH THE SLIDE REMOVED. FAILURE TO COMPLY WILL DAMAGE THE REAR OF THE FRAME.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER P211 — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — 5100230-01 — part number printed on the document — Field strip the pistol, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: ⛔ On older pistols the slide catch PIN stays put
deepSteps.action: If your P211 has a slide catch pin — SIG says these are the older pistols — do not remove it. Removing it may damage the firearm. When taking the ambidextrous catch off, older levers rotate about 50 degrees and newer ones 90; either way, make sure the pin does not fall out.
deepSteps.prose: Two generations, two rotation angles and one part that must not leave. Worth knowing which pistol is in your hands.
deepSteps.quote: IF PRESENT, DO NOT REMOVE THE SLIDE CATCH PIN. FAILURE TO COMPLY MAY RESULT IN DAMAGE TO THE FIREARM. THE SLIDE CATCH PIN IS PRESENT ON OLDER P211 PISTOLS.
deepSteps.cite: SIG SAUER P211 — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — 5100230-01 — part number printed on the document — Field strip the pistol, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Prove the magazine falls free — on a double stack it matters more
deepSteps.action: Insert an empty magazine, confirm the audible click and that the catch holds it, then press the catch and confirm the magazine falls free UNDER ITS OWN WEIGHT. A double-stack magazine in a 1911-pattern frame is the part most affected by fouling in the well.
deepSteps.prose: Under its own weight is the test. Helping it out is not passing.
deepSteps.aside: Grasp slide and pull it completely to the rear. The magazine follower should push up the slide catch lever, locking the slide to the rear.
deepSteps.quote: Press the magazine catch. The magazine must fall free under its own weight.
deepSteps.cite: SIG SAUER P211 — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — 5100230-01 — part number printed on the document — Function check, printed p.45

deepSteps.title: The function check is owed after every clean
deepSteps.action: SIG states the check is performed after repairs and after each time the pistol is cleaned and reassembled. If it fails, the manual's instruction is not to use the pistol and to contact customer service.
deepSteps.prose: Reassembly is where mistakes enter. That is why the check sits after it.
deepSteps.quote: The function check is performed on the assembled pistol to verify functionality. It should be performed after the completion of repairs and after each time the pistol is cleaned and reassembled.
deepSteps.cite: SIG SAUER P211 — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — 5100230-01 — part number printed on the document — Function check, printed p.45

cleaning.name: BARREL AND BORE
tasks: Patch and brush from the CHAMBER end until patches come out clean.
Clean the outside of the barrel, the locking lugs and the barrel link.

cleaning.name: SLIDE AND FRAME
tasks: Brush the breech face, extractor and slide rails; wipe with a lint-free cloth.
Clean the frame rails and the magazine well; a double-stack well collects more than a single-stack one.

cleaning.name: RECOIL SYSTEM
tasks: Wipe the recoil spring, guide rod and plug; inspect the spring for a loss of force or a set.
⚠ On older pistols, check the slide catch pin is still in place — it is not to be removed.

reassembly: Barrel into the slide, link rotated to clear; recoil plug in.
Recoil spring onto the guide rod, then spring and guide down over the barrel link and back into position.
Slide assembly onto the frame rails from the front, keeping hold of the spring guide.
Align the slide catch lug with the DISASSEMBLY notch and press the catch home from the left.
Release the slide forward and engage the manual safety.
⛔ Function-check — SIG requires it after each cleaning and reassembly.
fncheck: SIG requires the function check after every clean and reassembly. With the pistol CLEAR: insert an empty magazine and listen for the click — the catch must hold it. Disengage the manual safety, pull the slide fully to the rear and confirm the magazine follower pushes the slide catch up and locks the slide back. Press the magazine catch and confirm the magazine falls free under its own weight. Then work the manual safety in both directions and confirm it blocks the trigger.
